headline: 英倫舞台銀幕新作
context: 英國藝文圈這幾天有兩部新作值得一看。愛丁堡藝穗新戲《After Party》，講一位即將滿80歲的祖母薇薇安（Alison Peebles飾）辦完生日派對後，隔天就打算迎接死亡；劇評形容這齣戲對死亡主題著墨太晚，顯得有些雜亂。倫敦犯罪劇情片《Never Had a Chance》則把鏡頭對準西倫敦豪恩斯洛（Hounslow）的旁遮普裔社群，講兩名20多歲好友雷維與傑伊，人生因毒品交易糾纏在一起。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Traverse theatre, Edinburgh A grandmother welcomes her family to a birthday bash in a muddled play that addresses its key theme too late A celebratory family get-together leads to an almighty conflagration in Morna Young’s play. The birthday party reunion is a well-worn storytelling trope for explosive family reckonings – the Traverse featured another such party this time last year with Consumed, directed by Katie Posner , who helms this production, too. Co-created by Young and Alex Fthenakis, the twist here is that flamboyant matriarch Vivienne (Alison Peebles), known as “glam-ma” to her grandchildren, is throwing an 80th birthday party and then plans to die the very next day. She has terminal cancer so has arranged her death, although we are not told how she has managed that, given assisted dying is currently illegal in Scotland , as well as England and Wales. Is this a near or alternate future – or merely wishful thinking? Continue reading...
sources.title: After Party review – matters of life and death as flamboyant ‘glam-ma’ turns 80

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Two likely lads in their 20s deal with problematic lives that dramatically intersect in this persuasive London drama This gritty crime drama unfolds entirely within the Punjabi community in London’s Hounslow district, a plausible demographic situation in which white people are so peripheral to the story that they are little more than extras. In fact watching this well-crafted, if somewhat melodramatic, debut for director Jazz Bhalla makes one wonder why there aren’t more films made in the UK with entirely British Asian casts. Here, it doesn’t makes the film better or worse, but it certainly feels realistic and true to its milieu. The story revolves around two best friends in their 20s, Ravi (Amar Chaggar) and Jay (Jayant Singh), likely lads who spend a lot of time hanging out, getting high or drunk and ending nearly every sentence with the word “bro”. On the face of it, Jay seems like the one with a more stable situation at home, living with his middle-class parents; while Ravi, who has a criminal record due to a drug bust, lives in a bedsit and is estranged from his mother ever since his father died and she remarried, much to the chagrin of his bossy older sister (Parvinder Shergill). But Ravi manages to get a job working for a building supply merchant, which compels him to start waking up at dawn and considering the downside of always being hung over. Plus, he might be in with a chance with pretty fast-food vendor Sukhi (Tina Sharma), an ambitious young woman keen to get away from her alcoholic father and drug-dealing brother. Continue reading...
sources.title: Never Had a Chance review – a slice of gritty British Asian life with a side of drug dealing and addiction

thread_text:
英國藝文圈這幾天有兩部新作值得一看。

愛丁堡藝穗新戲《After Party》，講一位即將滿80歲的祖母薇薇安（Alison Peebles飾）辦完生日派對後，隔天就打算迎接死亡；劇評形容這齣戲對死亡主題著墨太晚，顯得有些雜亂。倫敦犯罪劇情片《Never Had a Chance》則把鏡頭對準西倫敦豪恩斯洛（Hounslow）的旁遮普裔社群，講兩名20多歲好友雷維與傑伊，人生因毒品交易糾纏在一起。

voice_text: 英國藝文圈，這幾天有兩部新作。愛丁堡藝穗新戲《After Party》，講一位快滿八十歲的祖母，辦完生日派對後，隔天就打算迎接死亡。劇評說，這齣戲對死亡主題，著墨得有點太晚。另一部倫敦犯罪劇情片，把鏡頭對準西倫敦一個旁遮普裔社群，講兩名二十多歲的好友，人生因為毒品交易糾纏在一起。
